newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes rate ends softer as peso stabilizes.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes rate ends softer as peso stabilizes.

text.p: Mexico's overnight Cetes rates closed down 125 basis points at 30.0 percent on Friday, in the wake of a more stable foreign exchange market.
"Although trading activity was quiet, overnight rates fell sharply," said a trader.
The 48-hour peso recouped more lost ground on Friday, and closed 2.7 centavos firmer at 7.9450/7.9530 per dollar.
Despite less pressure on secondary rates from the peso, traders said they still expected primary Cetes rates to increase slightly at next week's auction.

"Increases in wages and energy costs planned for December have modified inflation forecasts, so care needs to be taken that real returns payable on Cetes are still attractive," said a money market analyst.
"But if the peso and the outcome of U.S. elections (on November 5) are favorable, then next week could see the last hike for 28-day Cetes rates," another analyst said.
